name: Trường hợp đầu tiên tại Việt Nam (HCMUFA, 2023)
institution: HCMUFA — Ho Chi Minh City University of Fine Arts (Đại học Mỹ thuật Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh)
note: First publicly reported AI academic integrity enforcement case in Vietnam; student received 50% score deduction for AI-generated essay submission
dinh_nghia: This case represents the first publicly documented enforcement of academic integrity policy against AI-generated content in Vietnam. A student at HCMUFA (Ho Chi Minh City University of Fine Arts) submitted an essay that was identified as AI-generated (likely using ChatGPT or a similar tool) and received a 50% score deduction as a disciplinary measure. The case is significant as the first data point establishing that Vietnamese institutions were actively enforcing AI integrity policies before any national legal framework specifically addressed generative AI.
phan_loai: Violation category: AI-assisted dishonesty / gian lận (fraud) under the institution's academic integrity code. The submission involved presenting AI-generated text as the student's own work without disclosure — constituting misrepresentation of authorship. Under Decree 109/2022 terminology, this falls closest to 'gian lận' (fraud) though the decree does not explicitly name AI-generated content as a violation type.
lich_su_khai_niem: The case occurred in 2023, the first academic year following ChatGPT's November 2022 public release and following the March 2023 effective date of Decree 109/2022. It demonstrates that enforcement was already occurring at the institutional level even without explicit national legal provisions for AI-generated content — institutions interpreted their existing integrity codes to cover AI fraud under the general 'gian lận' (fraud) category.
ten_truong_hop: HCMUFA AI Essay Case (2023). Institution: Ho Chi Minh City University of Fine Arts (Trường Đại học Mỹ thuật Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh). Year: 2023. Reported by Vietnamese media (VietnamNet, Tuổi Trẻ) as the first AI integrity enforcement case in Vietnam.
dien_bien: A student submitted an essay assignment that faculty identified as AI-generated content, most likely generated using ChatGPT (the most widely available generative AI tool in Vietnam at the time). Detection method is not publicly confirmed — likely based on instructor judgment (stylistic inconsistency, atypical vocabulary, suspiciously polished output) rather than automated AI detection tools [uncertain detection method]. The institution applied a 50% score deduction penalty. The case received media attention as an example of Vietnamese universities grappling with AI integrity without a national policy framework. HCMUFA subsequently issued an explicit AI use policy [uncertain whether policy was formalized in writing].
ket_qua_xu_ly: Penalty: 50% score deduction applied to the student's submission. No expulsion or academic suspension reported. The case prompted internal policy discussions at HCMUFA. Media coverage positioned the case as a warning to other Vietnamese students about AI use in academic submissions. No formal appeal process outcome reported [uncertain]. The case influenced other Vietnamese universities to accelerate development of their own AI policies in 2023.
con_so_thong_ke: 1 confirmed case publicly reported; 50% score deduction (penalty); 2023 (year); 1 student affected in this specific case. Context: Vietnamese media reported a significant increase in student inquiries about AI use policies following this case. No national statistics on AI integrity violations in Vietnam are available [uncertain].
hai_cho_nguoi_hoc: The case illustrates the personal cost of AI fraud: the student lost 50% of their grade on the assignment, potentially affecting their academic standing, and faced the social consequences of being publicly associated with the first such case in Vietnam. More broadly, students who use AI without developing their own skills face genuine capability gaps that emerge at graduation or in employment — particularly relevant at a fine arts institution where authentic creative work is the core competency.
hai_cho_nghien_cuu: While this was a coursework submission rather than a research publication, the same dynamic applies to research: AI-generated content that misrepresents the author's intellectual contribution undermines the credibility of research outputs. In a fine arts context, AI-generated creative work submitted as original artwork raises additional questions about authorship and artistic integrity beyond standard academic integrity frameworks.
hai_cho_xa_hoi: The case received disproportionate media attention precisely because it was the first — signaling widespread public awareness and concern about AI fraud in Vietnamese education. The 50% penalty was seen as both too lenient by some commentators and too harsh by others, reflecting the absence of nationally standardized AI integrity penalties. The case may have normalized a lower-than-expulsion penalty as the default Vietnamese response to AI fraud.
cong_cu_phat_hien: Detection method: instructor judgment (most likely) — not automated AI detection tools [uncertain]. At the time of this case (early-mid 2023), Turnitin AI Detection had just launched (April 2023) and was not yet widely deployed in Vietnamese universities. GPTZero was available but use at HCMUFA is unconfirmed. This makes the case notable: detection was human-based, raising questions about consistency and scalability of such detection methods across Vietnamese HE.
han_che_cong_cu: Human-based detection (instructor judgment) is inconsistent and susceptible to bias — more confident or experienced instructors may detect AI writing that others miss. This creates an equity issue: students in courses with AI-literate instructors face higher detection risk than those in courses without such instructors, even for identical behavior. Vietnamese institutions' low adoption of automated detection tools exacerbates this inconsistency.
watermarking: Not applicable to this 2023 case — no watermarking technology was available or deployed. If LLM watermarking had been in place (e.g., if ChatGPT had implemented Aaronson's watermarking scheme in 2022), the detection would have been automatic and unambiguous rather than relying on instructor judgment.
thiet_ke_bai_tap: The HCMUFA case suggests that essay-based assessments are vulnerable to AI substitution even in creative/arts contexts. Process-based alternatives — portfolio submissions with documented creative process, studio observation, oral defense of work — would be both AI-resistant and more authentic for an arts curriculum. The case highlights the mismatch between traditional essay assessment and AI capabilities.
chinh_sach_truong_hoc: HCMUFA's response established a de facto policy through enforcement: a 50% penalty for AI-generated submissions. This was institution-specific and not based on an explicit written AI policy at the time [uncertain whether a written policy existed]. The case demonstrates the risk of enforcement-before-policy: students cannot be fully held accountable for violating a rule that was not clearly communicated in advance.
van_hoa_to_chuc: The case was handled punitively rather than educationally — a 50% deduction without public discussion of why AI fraud harms learning or the student's own development. A culture-based approach (McCabe model) would include the penalty alongside educational intervention: explaining the integrity values at stake and providing guidance on appropriate AI use going forward.
ai_literacy: The case reveals an AI literacy gap: the student either did not know that AI-generated submission was prohibited or did not expect to be detected. Both scenarios point to a need for explicit AI literacy education — covering not just what is prohibited but why, and how to use AI tools legitimately as learning aids. HCMUFA and Vietnamese universities more broadly should integrate AI literacy into academic integrity orientation.
khung_quoc_te: The HCMUFA case is consistent with first-wave AI enforcement cases internationally in 2023 (Texas A&M, Emory, Sheffield UK). The 50% deduction is a more lenient sanction than the expulsions reported at CUHK in 2023 or the zero marks at NTU in 2025. The case aligns with ICAI Honesty value (misrepresentation of work) and UNESCO GenAI guidance's acknowledgment that HEIs need clear student-facing policies.
phap_luat_viet_nam: The case occurred under the newly effective Decree 109/2022. HCMUFA's enforcement used the 'gian lận' (fraud) category to cover AI-generated submission — demonstrating that institutions can and do interpret existing law to cover AI fraud, even without explicit provisions. This sets a precedent that could inform MOET's guidance on applying Decree 109 to AI contexts.
chinh_sach_chau_a: Comparable cases in 2023 Asia: CUHK (Hong Kong) — expulsion for AI submission; NUS (Singapore) — zero marks + warning; Waseda (Japan) — policy issued without specific enforcement cases reported. HCMUFA's 50% deduction is a lighter sanction than most regional peers, suggesting Vietnamese enforcement is at the lenient end of the Asia spectrum.
ai_tutor_vs_ai_cheater: The HCMUFA case provides concrete evidence for the 'AI as cheater' framing: a student used AI not to enhance learning but to substitute their own intellectual work entirely. However, the case also raises the 'AI as tutor' question — if the student had used AI for drafting assistance and then substantially revised the output, would (or should) the same penalty apply? The lack of a nuanced policy framework makes such distinctions unenforceable.
edtech_company_policies: The AI tool used (likely ChatGPT / OpenAI) had no mechanism to flag or prevent academic submission of its outputs at the time of the case. OpenAI's since-retracted AI detection tool (Jan 2023, retired July 2023) was not deployed by HCMUFA. This illustrates the gap between EdTech company capabilities and institutional enforcement needs.
de_xuat_nha_nghien_cuu: As an EdTech researcher: (1) Document Vietnamese cases systematically — the HCMUFA case is the only publicly known one, but institutional cases are almost certainly underreported; (2) Advocate for a national case registry (similar to the US Office of Research Integrity database) to enable pattern analysis; (3) Use this case to argue for explicit written AI policies before enforcement, not after — students need fair notice; (4) Recommend that penalty structures be nationally standardized (tiered: warning → partial deduction → fail grade → suspension) to avoid arbitrary enforcement; (5) HCMUFA's fine arts context makes process-based assessment (documented creative process, portfolio) an especially strong alternative to essay-based assessment.
bai_bao_khoa_hoc: Nguyen et al. (2024) Springer — AI cheating prevalence Vietnamese undergraduates (doi:10.1007/s10639-024-12495-4) — provides statistical context for this case. No peer-reviewed analysis of the HCMUFA case specifically identified [uncertain].
sach_tham_khao: Eaton, S.E. (2024) Second Handbook of Academic Integrity — chapters on emerging AI cases. Vietnamese media archives: VietnamNet, Tuổi Trẻ, Thanh Niên (2023 reporting on first AI integrity cases).
